blocking.finding: `overlap_context_block` renders candidate fields using keys that the retrieval results never contain. Both `search()` (lexical) and `rank()` (embedding) return dicts keyed `id`/`alias`/`title`/`score` — never `ticket_id`, `status`, or `state`. So the `c.get('ticket_id')` fallback is dead (a candidate with an empty alias renders `?` instead of its `id`), and the status column is ALWAYS `?`.
blocking.suggested_fix: Use `alias = c.get('alias') or c.get('id') or '?'` and remove the status term (or enrich candidates with a real status before rendering), since the retrieval dicts carry no status.

Similar subject matter is not overlap: flag only where the two plans would produce the same change. Name the ticket you mean. If none overlaps, say nothing.")
This text is injected as finder (Pass-1) context via overlap_context_block / _chunk_extra_context in pass1.py, so it is an operative instruction to the Pass-1 phase.

Instructed phase: Pass 1 (finder). Assigned action: judging/deciding whether the plan is a true overlap ('judge whether... produce the same change'). Owning phase: Pass 2 (independent verification of validity).
dropped.finding: The injected finder directive instructs the Pass-1 finder to perform a validity determination — 'Judge whether THIS plan does work a listed ticket already describes' and 'flag only where the two plans would produce the same change' — which is the atomic-validity work owned by Pass 2, not candidate discovery owned by Pass 1.
scenarios: A finder reads this directive and withholds a grounded candidate because it has already concluded the overlap is invalid, pre-empting Pass 2's verification.
